text.original_context: Lab notebook, week 3. At sea level, pure water freezes at 0 degrees Celsius and boils at 100 degrees Celsius. Air pressure is lower at high altitude, so water boils below 100 degrees Celsius there. Boiling turns liquid water into water vapour; the temperature stays at the boiling point until the liquid is gone.
text.original_input: At what temperature does water boil, and why do people say it boils sooner in the mountains?
